code_paper_alignment.methodology_describ.reason: The Methodology describes what the code does. Covariance: K = sigma_f^2 (K_T kron K_G) + sigma_n^2 I with time-major vectorization. Polynomial: W(u) = (1-u)^8 (32u^3 + 25u^2 + 8u + 1) in both the paper's equation and traffic_kernels.py. The stock Wendland is applied separably, and the paper says so. Every Nelder-Mead/BMH evaluation uses the exact Kronecker eigen-likelihood on all 500,112 observations. Optimization: 35 Nelder-Mead iterations (maxiter 35, log message confirms the limit was hit), then 20 cycles of 3 blocks (60 proposals) with the stated block structure, keeping the highest-likelihood accepted state. Assembly: Dask block assembly requesting 8 workers; the paper says 'requested', and the log shows 5 registered addresses and 15/18 blocks. Solves: fvGP sparse CG and the SLQ log-determinant are called. Prediction uses the exact eigensystem. Vecchia: the described predecessor set and Matérn-3/2 recurrent kernel, with 3,539 patterns. Harmonic mean: training-only, as stated. Two points are unverifiable but not contradictory. The paper credits the 32-coefficient polynomial to fvGP; fvGP's source is not in the staged snapshot, and the paper's formula matches the submitted code. The MNIST code clips predictions to [0,1] without saying so, but I verified the clip changes nothing. No material contradiction.

baseline_honesty.baseline_genuine_best_e.reason: Vecchia: trained at the full 500,112 points with 30 predecessors (the original paper's default). Its predecessor set includes directed-upstream and previous-day same-phase neighbors, and its kernel has the same compact daily recurrence DIR uses. Three jittered initializations all converged to the same optimum (approximate LL -1,414,660.38). The noise and spatial-length lower-bound hits are disclosed in the paper and the attempts log, and Vecchia wins RMSE, which is reported. Existing-kernel Wendland: given the same initial signal and noise variance and the same 35 Nelder-Mead + 60 BMH budget as DIR. The preregistered 5e8 sparsity cap never fired (0 rejections), and the learned supports are interior to their bounds (0.585 km within [0.5, 10]; 29.38 frames within [2.1, 60]). Its signal variance did reach the shared upper bound of 400 (399.48; 6 out-of-bounds BMH proposals rejected), and the paper does not mention this. The same bound applies to all three models and was set before any run. Relaxing it would raise Wendland's already 20.26 mph prior SD, so it would not narrow DIR's CRPS or calibration advantage. Limited tuning and a shared bound are not affirmative evidence of deliberate weakening.
